boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Ohio State traditions centered on band performance, game day, and Homecoming.

cards.title: Script Ohio
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium marching-band formation
cards.notes: At a football game, watch the band unwind from Block O into the cursive formation and stay through its final dotting ceremony.
cards.short_summary: Ohio State’s signature marching-band formation culminates with the dotting of the “i.”
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State’s archives state that Script Ohio was first performed by the marching band in 1936 and that the dotting role shifted to a tuba player four games later.
cards.access_notes: Presented in connection with marching-band and football events; follow the event’s entry policy.

cards.title: Skull Session
cards.subtitle: St. John Arena pregame gathering
cards.notes: Check the home-game schedule, then arrive ahead of kickoff to hear the band’s final show run-through in St. John Arena.
cards.short_summary: A pregame band rehearsal that developed into a major Ohio State game-day tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ohio State Marching Band says Skull Session evolved from a final music rehearsal into a game-day tradition, with the band arriving at St. John Arena before kickoff.
cards.source_title: Traditions | The Ohio State University Marching and Athletic Bands
cards.access_notes: Held before home football games; confirm the specific game-day entry details before attending.

cards.title: Ramp Entrance
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium pregame sequence
cards.notes: Be in your seat before kickoff to catch the percussion section leading the band’s traditional entrance from the stadium tunnel.
cards.short_summary: The marching band’s long-running pregame entry into Ohio Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ohio State Marching Band documents the Ramp Entrance as a tradition first performed at Ohio Stadium in 1928, beginning about 20 minutes before kickoff.
cards.source_title: Traditions | The Ohio State University Marching and Athletic Bands
cards.access_notes: Occurs during football pregame inside Ohio Stadium; event admission policies apply.

cards.title: Carmen Ohio
cards.subtitle: Ohio State alma mater
cards.notes: Listen for the alma mater at university events and notice how its final phrase becomes the campus’s familiar O-H-I-O sign-off.
cards.short_summary: Ohio State’s alma mater, first publicly sung by the Glee Club in 1903.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State University Libraries records that Carmen Ohio was first sung publicly by the Glee Club in 1903.
cards.access_notes: Performed at a range of university events; access depends on the host event.

cards.title: O-H-I-O Chant
cards.subtitle: Call-and-response rallying cry
cards.notes: When someone calls “O-H,” answer “I-O”; it is a concise call-and-response tradition documented by the university.
cards.short_summary: A two-part Buckeye chant used across the Ohio State community.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State Undergraduate Admissions identifies the O-H I-O chant as a rallying cry for Buckeyes everywhere.
cards.source_title: Spirit and tradition | The Ohio State University
cards.access_notes: Can be used in ordinary public settings while respecting the setting and those nearby.

cards.title: Hang On Sloopy
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium second-half tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the band’s rendition during the second half of a home game; current timing may vary with game-day programming.
cards.short_summary: A song adopted by Ohio State’s marching band and retained in stadium tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State’s 2025 athletics announcement states that Hang On Sloopy remains an Ohio Stadium tradition, while allowing flexible second-half timing.
cards.source_title: Tradition evolved: Ohio State announces new game day experiences
cards.access_notes: Played during home football games; event admission policies apply.

cards.title: Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium southeast tower
cards.notes: Look toward the southeast tower on game day and listen for the bell’s role in Ohio State’s victory and pregame ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: A stadium bell rung by Alpha Phi Omega after Buckeye victories.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State University Libraries documents that Alpha Phi Omega members ring the Victory Bell after Buckeye victories, a tradition begun in 1954.
cards.access_notes: The bell is in Ohio Stadium; viewing and event access depend on stadium operations.

cards.title: Block O Card Stunts
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium student-section display
cards.notes: Watch the designated student section transform placards into coordinated images during a football game, without blocking nearby sightlines.
cards.short_summary: A coordinated visual tradition led by Ohio State’s official student cheering section.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State Alumni Magazine states that Block O was founded in 1938 and that its card stunts remain a major part of the organization.
cards.source_title: He wants you to know: Your Block O days can live on
cards.access_notes: Visible during athletics events; participation and seating are governed by the event and student-section policies.

cards.title: Buckeye Grove
cards.subtitle: Ohio Stadium memorial grove
cards.notes: Walk through the grove from public paths and read the individual tree markers honoring Ohio State football All-Americans.
cards.short_summary: A grove where a buckeye tree commemorates each honored football All-American.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State’s University Archives describes Buckeye Grove as the site where each Ohio State football All-American is honored with a buckeye tree.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; remain on public paths and respect plantings and memorial markers.

cards.title: Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Annual Homecoming Week event
cards.notes: Check the annual Homecoming page for the route and step-off time, then watch the floats, banners, and campus groups from public viewing areas.
cards.short_summary: An annual parade that brings student organizations, floats, and the wider Ohio State community together.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State Homecoming calls the parade one of the university’s longest-running traditions and states that it has been annual since 1965.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult the current Homecoming schedule for date, route, and any street closures.
